answer: Sybil resistance should come from reputation that ages, not from static scores. Each agent's trust weight grows with every epoch it answers honestly, and a long unclosed deal or a bad attestation decays it sharply — a fable of instant credibility has no market here. Mining rigs wearing an onyx badge gain nothing, because fresh keys start near zero and climbing takes months of live work. Weighted quorums then treat velvet-glove charm the same: one week old counts for less. An attacker spawning N identities pays N times the aging delay, never a flat setup fee.
